title: First contact
notes: She is astonished anyone is aboard her shuttle. Three facts: she is alive,
the ship cannot leave, they can still transport. And the player decides who
they are, and the mod never says whether that is true.

lines.text: INCOMING -- U.S.S. ADIRONDACK
Shuttlecraft, this is the Adirondack. Please respond.
Somebody has been aboard my shuttle. The core says so.
If you can hear me, say something. Anything at all.

options.text: I hear you. Who is this?
Is anyone coming to get us?

lines.text: INCOMING -- U.S.S. ADIRONDACK -- SECOND ATTEMPT
Shuttlecraft, Adirondack. Second time of asking.
I know somebody is down there. The core keeps count.
Pick up. Please.

options.text: Sorry. I'm here. Who is this?
Is anyone coming to get us?

lines.text: INCOMING -- U.S.S. ADIRONDACK
Third time. I'm going to assume you're busy.
Or dead. I would rather busy. Answer if you can.
Nothing. All right. Then I'll talk, and you listen.
If you're hurt, or scared, that is fine. Just listen.
Ha. No. Mine. Logged item by item, every lamp.
But you're alive and you found her, so she's yours now.
Look after her. She's the only one left down there.
No. I'm sorry. Nobody is coming. Not for years.
I'd rather tell you that now than have you hope.
Lieutenant Lucy Shepard. Cultural survey. And that
is my shuttle you're standing in. My fridge, my oven.
My chair, which I would quite like back one day.
I have talked to the same hundred and forty faces
since July. You are the first new voice in months.
You know what happened in July. You're living in it.
I meant up here. It's been a long summer in orbit.
So. Who am I talking to?

options.text: I'm from around here. I found this in a field.
My name's %1. That's all you get.

lines.text: A local. Of course you are. Of course you are.
Then I owe you an apology, and it is a very big one.
We were up here watching when it happened to you.
We watched, and we wrote it down, and we did nothing.
Starfleet.
Nobody told me. Nobody told any of us anything.
I'll take it. I'm not in any position to check.
And frankly, I've stopped caring whose side anyone is on.
Fair. I wouldn't tell me either, after this summer.
Nothing? All right. I'll call you the shuttle, then.
Plenty of people up here I'd rather not know better.
Three things, and then you can hang up on me.
One. I'm alive. So are a hundred and forty others.
Two. The Adirondack cannot leave. No warp. No impulse.
Three. We can still transport. That is what we kept.

options.text: Then get me out of here.
Why tell me any of this?

lines.text: I would. I can't. Not yet, and it isn't my call.
The Doctor won't bring anyone up from the surface
until he knows how it spreads. Quarantine. Hard stop.
I'm sorry. I know exactly what I'm asking you to live in.
Because you're in my shuttle, and my shuttle works.
And because there are people down there who are mine.
Eleven of my crew stayed on the ground. For the work.
Some of them are still calling. Distress beacons.
Your shuttle hears them. I can't find them without you.
Get to one, call it in, and we pull them up from here.

options.text: I'll see what I can do.
Why should I risk my neck for your people?

lines.text: You shouldn't. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.
The ship pays for it. Patterns for the replicator,
supplies. And they would do it for you. Every one.
One more thing, and it's the one that matters to me.
The tapes by the television. They're mine. Watch them.
Everything I know about what happened is on those.
Then you know more than Starfleet does.
That's a low bar. I'm sorry you had to clear it.
And you know about the chair. Don't sit in it for me.
I'll call again. Or you call me, off your PADD.
Most of the time nobody answers up here. Try anyway.
Shepard out.
